description: I’m a student interested in space, games, and technology. I’m building Lunar Outpost: Rover Rescue, an interactive game that helps kids explore life on the Moon. I’m looking for teammates with skills in game development, 3D art, design, storytelling, or space science to help make the game fun, polished, and accurate.
summary:
**Lunar Outpost: Rover Rescue** is an interactive 3D mission game that puts players in control of a rover at a lunar base. Players complete story-based missions: clean solar panels, repair a water recycler, respond to a simulated space-weather warning, restore communications, and prepare the habitat for lunar night. A minimap, clear in-game instructions, a robot companion, sound effects, and rover collisions help make the outpost feel active and navigable.

The project addresses the challenge by giving younger players a hands-on way to explore decisions astronauts may face while living and working on the Moon. It makes space science approachable through play, while showing how power, supplies, safety, and communication connect in a mission.
details:
Lunar Outpost: Rover Rescue is a browser-based 3D game for ages 7–12. Players drive a rover through five lunar missions, responding to problems such as dusty solar panels, a clogged recycler, and a simulated space-weather alert. Completing tasks earns Moon Coins, while player choices affect the outpost’s power, supplies, and safety. A companion character, mission instructions, sound effects, collisions, and a map help players follow the story and navigate.

The project aims to make lunar exploration and the systems that support astronauts easier for young audiences to understand through interactive play. It was built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js, using KayKit 3D assets and NASA resources for context. We considered the 7–12 age group, clear instructions, accessible controls, and the difference between a simulated game alert and real space-weather information.
